issues.display_title: Issue #4059: Add Shareable Google Link as Photographer Portfolio
issues.main_description_html:
Brainstorming File: 2026-06-02-pano-info-photographer-portfolio-buttons-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

AC-1: Add as Portfolio button visibility — photographer user

  • Given the user has applied to or been approved for the photographer directory (state.profile.photographer !== null)
  • And the Google Info card has a share_link value
  • And the tour is not archived
  • Then an "Add as Portfolio" button (blue/primary) appears in the footer after "Copy Share Link"]

AC-2: Add as Portfolio button hidden — non-photographer user

  • Given the user has NOT applied to the photographer directory (state.profile.photographer === null)
  • Then the "Add as Portfolio" button is not rendered, even if a share link exists

AC-3: Add as Portfolio button hidden when no share link

  • Given the user is a photographer
  • And the pano has no share_link
  • Then the "Add as Portfolio" button is not rendered

AC-4: Add as Portfolio action — success

  • Given the "Add as Portfolio" button is visible
  • When the user clicks it
  • Then POST /photographers/portfolio/save is called with { title: <panorama_name>, value: <share_link>, type: 'google' }
  • And the button shows a loading spinner while the request is in flight
  • And on success a toast confirms the save
  • And the entry appears in the Google Street View section of /photographer/portfolio

AC-5: Add as Portfolio action — error

  • When the API call fails
  • Then a toast error message is shown
  • And the button returns to its default state (no spinner)

Demo from Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #4060: Implement Virtual Tour Manager Menu on Virtual Tour Dropdown at My Tour
issues.main_description_html:
Brainstorming File: 2026-06-02-virtual-tour-manager-dropdown-item-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

AC-1: Menu item is present

  • Given a tour card with an active virtual tour (dropdown is visible)
  • When the user opens the Virtual Tour dropdown
  • Then "Virtual Tour Manager" appears as the last item in the menu

AC-2: Menu item order

  • Then the order is: View Virtual Tour → View Google Virtual Tour → Edit Virtual Tour → Virtual Tour Manager

AC-3: Shown only if the tour has a main overlay.json file

  • Given a tour where overlay_active is false AND goverlay_active is false
  • When the dropdown is opened (if it is shown by its parent logic)
  • Then "Virtual Tour Manager" still appears — it has no conditional guard

AC-4: Navigation on click

  • When the user clicks "Virtual Tour Manager"
  • Then the app navigates to /my-tours/:mid/hosted using internal SPA routing (no full page reload)
  • And the Virtual Tour Manager page loads for the correct tour

AC-5: Correct tour context

  • Given two different tour cards, each with their own mid
  • When the user clicks "Virtual Tour Manager" on either card
  • Then each navigates to its own /my-tours//hosted — not a shared or hardcoded ID

AC-6: Existing items unaffected

  • Then "View Virtual Tour", "View Google Virtual Tour", and "Edit Virtual Tour" behave exactly as before
  • And their visibility conditions (overlay_active, goverlay_active) are unchanged

AC-7: Localization key present

  • Given the app is running in any supported locale
  • Then the "Virtual Tour Manager" label renders correctly (not as a raw key string)

issues.display_title: Issue #4061: Bug Fix Photographer Main Location Not Saving
issues.main_description_html:
Task Description

Brainstorming File: 2026-06-02-photographer-location-save-fix-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

AC-1: No crash on first visit (no location record)

  • Given a newly submitted user who has never set a main location
  • When the /photographer/location page loads
  • Then executeGetLocation handles a null or missing location field gracefully — no silent TypeError
  • And the form renders in an empty state (no location on map, search field blank)
  • And hasMainLocation is false

AC-2: No crash when location is 0,0

  • Given the API returns { latitude: 0, longitude: 0 } for a user
  • When the page loads
  • Then the zero-location branch resets state (same behavior as AC-1) without crashing

AC-3: Save + backend persistence confirmed — happy path

  • Given the user selects a valid location via Google Places
  • When the user clicks the save button
  • And the PATCH API returns HTTP 200 and the GET re-fetch returns the saved coordinates
  • Then a success toast appears
  • And hasMainLocation becomes true
  • And the map and search field reflect the saved location

AC-4: Save returns 200 but backend did not persist — silent failure detected

  • Given the PATCH API returns HTTP 200 (success toast fires)
  • But the subsequent GET re-fetch returns null or 0,0 (backend did not actually save)
  • Then hasMainLocation is reset to false
  • And the form resets to empty — the user can see the save did not stick

AC-5: Re-fetch runs automatically after save

  • Given a successful save (PATCH 200)
  • Then executeGetLocation is called immediately after the success toast
  • And hasMainLocation is only set to true by the re-fetch result, not by the save handler directly

AC-6: Save API error handled correctly

  • Given the PATCH API returns a non-200 response
  • Then an error toast shows res.data.details or res.data.messages
  • And executeGetLocation is NOT re-called
  • And hasMainLocation remains unchanged

AC-7: Subsequent visit shows saved location

  • Given a user who successfully saved a location (AC-3 confirmed)
  • When they navigate away and return to /photographer/location
  • Then executeGetLocation loads and displays the saved coordinates and address
  • And hasMainLocation is true

AC-8: Sub-location and existing behavior unchanged

  • Then sub-location save, delete, and load behavior is unaffected
  • And the floppy-disk save button position and appearance are unchanged
  • And onSelectLocation (Google Places selection) and onSetLocationByLatLng (lat/lng input) behave exactly as before

Note by Developer

After testing it, it seems this is an API issue because while the API returns a success response when saving the address, the location field is still empty when retrieving the data via the API.

issues.display_title: Issue #4064: Bug Fix Missing View Virtual Tour and View Google View Virtual Tour in Virtual Tour Menu at My Tour
issues.main_description_html:
Brainstorming File: 2026-06-03-virtual-tour-dropdown-fix-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

  • A tour with overlay_active: true (and no has_main_overlay) shows the dropdown button with only "View Virtual Tour"
  • A tour with goverlay_active: true (and no has_main_overlay) shows the dropdown button with only "View Google Virtual Tour"
  • A tour with has_main_overlay: true (and no active overlays) shows the dropdown button with "Edit Virtual Tour" and "Virtual Tour Manager" — no view items
  • A tour with all three flags true shows all 4 items
  • A tour with all three flags false shows no dropdown button
  • "View Virtual Tour" navigates to the gothru hosted overlay URL (getTourLink(item, 'F1')) in a new tab
  • "View Google Virtual Tour" navigates to the Google overlay URL (getTourLink(item, 'G1')) in a new tab
  • "Edit Virtual Tour" opens the overlay editor via openOverlayEditor(item.tour_key)
  • "Virtual Tour Manager" navigates to /my-tours/${item.moderation_id}/hosted
  • Menu items always render in order: View Virtual Tour → View Google Virtual Tour → Edit Virtual Tour → Virtual Tour Manager (items that don't meet their condition are simply absent, not reordered)
  • Both grid view (TourCard) and list view (ToursTable) reflect the corrected button visibility

Note from Developer

The “View Google Virtual Tour” and “View Virtual Tour” menus have been running like this since the beginning.. To display them, you must first activate the main virtual tour. Here's how to display them:

I checked the reported tour, and it's likely that the main tour hasn't been activated yet. I even checked and the tour (overlay.json) doesn't even exist yet.
